mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates economic growth, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) stimulates borrowing and investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are negative when FEDFUNDS is below 0.15.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (high UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are negative when unemployment is low.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production (INDPRO) signals economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are negative when industrial production grows.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are negative when housing starts grow.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL) may lead to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are positive when inflation is high.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in employment (PAYEMS) alongside a decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns do not correlate with the joint movement of PAYEMS and UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are negative when retail sales grow.
